MOLECULAR CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Cancer Center

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Specimen Type: Thigh mass biopsy
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Thigh mass biopsy submitted for molecular cytogenetic analysis

TEST PERFORMED
Interphase Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) Analysis

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed on paraffin-embedded tissue sections correlated with CD20 immunostained slides. A total of 100 cells were analyzed for the following rearrangements:
• IGH/MALT1 t(14;18) rearrangement using IGH/MALT1 dual fusion FISH probe kit
• BIRC3(API2)/MALT1 t(11;18) rearrangement using BIRC3(API2)/MALT1 dual fusion FISH probe kit

Probe specifications:
- IGH probe (14q32): SpectrumGreen
- MALT1 probe (18q21): SpectrumOrange
- BIRC3(API2) probe (11q22): SpectrumGreen

RESULTS

IGH/MALT1 t(14;18) Analysis:
Result: NEGATIVE
No evidence of IGH/MALT1 rearrangement detected
Pattern: 2G2O (two green IGH signals, two orange MALT1 signals) in 97/100 cells analyzed

BIRC3(API2)/MALT1 t(11;18) Analysis:
Result: NEGATIVE
No evidence of BIRC3(API2)/MALT1 rearrangement detected
Pattern: 2G3O (two green BIRC3 signals, three orange MALT1 signals) in 96/100 cells analyzed

ADDITIONAL FINDING:
Three copies of MALT1 locus (18q21) identified in 96% of cells analyzed
This finding is suggestive of trisomy 18

INTERPRETATION
FISH analysis demonstrates no evidence of t(14;18) IGH/MALT1 or t(11;18) BIRC3(API2)/MALT1 rearrangements, which are recurrent translocations associated with MALT lymphoma. However, three copies of the MALT1 locus were identified, suggestive of trisomy 18. This abnormal finding may be relevant for lymphoma diagnosis or classification. The absence of MALT1 rearrangements with the presence of an extra copy of chromosome 18 should be correlated with morphologic and immunophenotypic findings.

TEST LIMITATIONS
This assay detects only the specific rearrangements tested. Other genetic abnormalities associated with lymphoma would not be detected by this analysis.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
